decisions.reason: F3 falsely attributes smooth composition and square-root regularity to a theorem of first one-variable derivative rules. Added the one-variable chain rule and ordered-partial definition, proved square-root regularity by rationalization and coordinate-line induction, and exhibited ambient slice charts. The rank-one determinant, Hessian determinant and finite AComega partition are valid; the Statement is unchanged.

The all-L1 chain of inequalities used an L2 quotient norm without L2 membership; on S1 the density |theta|^(-3/4) is integrable but not square integrable. Split the universally valid L1 transform bound from the additional bound for g in L2, whose inclusion in L1 follows from Holder with the finite-measure constant function. Extension, linearity, uniform continuity, Schwartz restriction and the conditional meaning of R are preserved.

F2 attributed the product rule to a total-derivative theorem that supplies only sums and scalar multiples. Added the actual one-variable product/quotient theorem and the partial/total bridges; step 1.1 derives Cr product, quotient and composition closure by coordinate-line induction before using the adjugate inverse bootstrap. Positive-square-root smoothness follows from that bootstrap on t squared. Slice-to-graph, normal invariance, self-adjointness and finite compact localization remain valid with the exact Statement unchanged.

The original proof applied a global stationary-phase interface to a phase defined only on the unit ball and explicitly dispensed with extension. Constructed a positive smooth radial derivative a and its primitive A so epsilon A(|y| squared) agrees on the amplitude support and has exactly one global critical point, with Hessian minus epsilon I. Zero extension makes amplitudes globally compact and smooth; adding and subtracting a bump meets the support-interior hypothesis. The finite sum and small-frequency decay claim are unchanged.

The null-sphere witness is valid: G equals the Schwartz transform ambient almost everywhere and differs by one on every sphere point. However the last step and explanatory ending asserted a bounded restriction extension for arbitrary 1<p<2 without a restriction estimate. Both now state the required bound explicitly and cite the exact conditional duality interface. The core refuted claim and witness remain intact; neither Hausdorff-Young nor density alone is used to infer restriction boundedness.

F3 used the existential concentration interface as though it guaranteed the prescribed numeric box. Chose a witness a_n from the actual Statement and set c_n=a_n/sqrt(n-1), explicitly proving tangential and normal containment. Cap measure and box volume yield the same exponent obstruction for every finite q; p=1 is automatic, finite p>1 follows by duality, and compact smooth norm tests rule out p=infinity. Replaced an unneeded monotone-cutoff assertion with monotone convergence on increasing balls. Statement unchanged. Additional confirmed citation defect: F4 cited integer-power laws for real exponents. Replaced that supplier with the real-power laws, explicit exponential/logarithm definitions and exponential limits. The p=infinity pairing now uses the finite cap measure and a Schwartz frequency cutoff, exactly matching the pairing interface.

The original box constant was not guaranteed by the cited existential tube interface. Retained the cap witness and all exponent claims, chose its box constant from a positive witness a_n, and proved sqrt(n-1)c_n=a_n and c_n<=a_n at step 1.1. The volume remains a positive dimension-dependent multiple of delta^(-(n+1)), so the negative power forces divergence. Finite restriction exponents use the duality hypothesis correctly, and p=infinity uses the assigned Knapp theorem. Also replaced the unsupported attribution of the negative-real-power limit to the Knapp Statement with its explicit exponential/logarithm argument and exact suppliers.

The example fixed every 0<c<=1/(100sqrt(n-1)), whereas the cited Statement gives only an unspecified tube constant. Preserved that full range and derived its concentration directly: |x prime|<=delta^(-1)/100, |omega prime|<=sqrt(2)delta and |omega_n-1|<=delta squared yield |2pi x dot (omega-e_n)|<1/2. The cosine lower bound integrates to sigma(cap)/2. Exact cap integral, equator caveat at delta=1, box volume, norm powers and q=infinity lower bound remain valid.
